text:
Andrei Svechnikov opened the season scoring, then went at least nine games without a goal before beating Semyon Varlamov on Thursday. Five points in his last ten is a cold stretch for a top-six wing on the defending champions, and it would be easy to call it a slump.

We'd read it differently. Across the season he is generating 1.56 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, well up on last season's 1.27, and Carolina owns 61% of the five-on-five chances with him on. His 13.7% shooting is dead normal. The dry spell came from fewer chances in a ten-game window (2.6 expected goals against his usual 4.1), not from a broken shot.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season fits the pattern: his team created plenty with him out there, but the finishing behind him lagged, and he gave some back defensively. He is also a physical presence, with 37 hits. Our projection still has him around 31 goals. If the volume keeps up, Thursday looks more like a start than an exception.
headline: Svechnikov's quiet October deserves a closer look
